title: git-vouch-migrate port: person-file drafts from pgpkeys@C
description: Separate tool (METARULE 2), the only one that runs gpg. Imports keys/*.asc from a pgpkeys checkout pinned at commit C into a temp GNUPGHOME and writes unsigned person-file drafts: handle derivation rule with deterministic collision handling, names decoded defensively (one UID is Latin-1), emails from unrevoked UIDs, migratedFrom openpgp4fpr:<40hex>, one draft per person (13 people hold two keys: merge or pick, documented), skip non-person keys (26 remail/security list keys). Also pre-derives SSH keys for holders whose GPG auth subkey is ed25519/P-256 (gpg --export-ssh-key).
acceptance_criteria: Run against ~/GIT/pgpkeys@af88128 produces ~606 drafts; counts reported match the research (645 live keys, 26 non-person, 93 reusable auth subkeys); every draft validates with git-vouch record validation (minus signature).
notes: Lane C-migrate 2026-10-22: implementation in git-vouch-migrate (port subcommand) reviewed and finished; tests in tests/migrate/ (16, real gpg/ssh-keygen/git on synthetic keyrings + real Latin-1 colon vector from pgpkeys). Acceptance run vs ~/GIT/pgpkeys@af88128 --signer DE0E66E32F1FDD0902666B96E63EDCA9329DD07E (Konstantin primary; B6C41CE35664996C is his signing subkey): keys 662, live 646, kernel.org list keys 26 (19 live), people 605, drafts 605, reusable auth 94; all 605 drafts pass git-vouch parse_record, 0 duplicate emails. Delta vs research (645 live / 93 auth) is exactly one key, DED396B8...B836 (Alan Maguire), which expired between C's committer date 2026-10-20 and today; judged at today's clock the counts are 645/93. Fixed: C's signature is now also judged at C (faked-system-time in temp gpg.conf), so an expiring signer does not break the port. Merge rule: keys sharing any email are one person (22 keys merged into 21 people), drafted from the newest key. Not closed (later stage closes).
